epigraph: Light does not ask. It only shows.
vignette: The scout held the lantern low. It was a seed of glass and gold light. It floated above the mud. The mud was old and gray. It remembered a wolf. It did not remember the tree. The seed hovered. It did not touch the ground. It cast a circle of bright white light. The circle pushed back the dark. The dark was the Umbral hunger. The light showed the path. It showed the cracks in the stone. It showed the roots of the old glass forest. The soldier watched the light. He knew the truth here was fragile. If he stepped in the dark, the ground would eat him. The lantern led the way. It was a small sun. It burned cold. It made the path real for one step. Then the next step. The army followed the light. They did not look back. The light was the only thing that was true. It was a promise of the Verdant permanence. It held the dark at bay with sheer conviction.
codex_note: The Lantern proves that visibility is the first act of territorial claim.
